title: Ship Thickness Measurement in Italy | UTM at Italian Ports
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement for ships in Italy: hull, tank and piping gauging at Genoa, Trieste, Naples, Venice, La Spezia, Palermo and other ports.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships in Italy
intro: Italy has more commercially active ports than any other Mediterranean country, strung along the Ligurian, Tyrrhenian, Ionian and Adriatic coasts and out to Sicily and Sardinia. Ships are gauged where they call: container and shiprepair berths at Genoa and La Spezia, refinery and chemical terminals at Augusta, Milazzo and Ravenna, ferry and cruise turnarounds at Naples and Civitavecchia, and transhipment at Gioia Tauro. Atlantis NDT mobilises its team from India to the vessel for each job, and plans ultrasonic thickness measurement around the ship's schedule and the docking date.

highlights.p: Genoa, Palermo, Naples, Trieste and other ports have ship repair facilities close to deep-water berths. Gauging the hull and tanks before the ship goes in turns the survey allowance into a measured steel list.

Sicily's east coast, Sardinia and the Adriatic carry heavy product and chemical tanker traffic. Cargo and ballast tanks are gauged after cleaning and gas-freeing, with readings located frame by frame.

highlights.h: The whole coast is an emission control area
highlights.p: Italian waters sit inside the Mediterranean emission control area, so scrubber ships are common. Wash-water and overboard piping is gauged for wall loss, a recurring finding on ships a few years into scrubber service.

sections.h: Where ships are gauged in Italy
p: In the north-west, Genoa and Savona-Vado, with La Spezia and the marble port of Marina di Carrara, serve the Ligurian arc. Genoa combines container and general cargo berths with a ship repair zone inside the port, and La Spezia handles containers and has a naval and shipbuilding history. Livorno and Piombino on the Tuscan coast add cargo, ferry and steel trades, and Civitavecchia is the main cruise gateway to Rome.

South of Rome, Naples and Salerno handle containers, ferries and cruise ships, while Castellammare di Stabia on the Bay of Naples has a historic yard. Gioia Tauro in Calabria is a deep-water transhipment hub. Sicily has the refinery bay at Augusta, the petrochemical berths at Milazzo, the passenger and cargo ports of Catania, Messina and Trapani, and Palermo with its repair yard. Sardinia adds Cagliari and Porto Torres.

On the Adriatic, Trieste at the head of the sea serves central Europe and the oil pipeline into Austria and Germany, Venice and Chioggia serve the lagoon and Marghera industrial zone, Ravenna handles bulk and chemical cargoes, and Ancona, Ortona, Bari, Brindisi and Taranto run along the eastern shore and the Ionian arc, each with its own cargo mix.

sections.h: The traffic behind the inspection demand
p: Italy's economy is built on imports of energy and raw materials and exports of manufactured goods, so tankers, bulk carriers, container ships and ro-ro ships all call in volume. Product and chemical tankers cluster at Augusta, Milazzo, Ravenna, Trieste and Genoa; bulk carriers serve steel and cement ports such as Taranto and Piombino; and ferries and cruise ships keep Naples, Civitavecchia, Palermo and Cagliari busy.

Because ships calling in Italy range from new tonnage to ageing coastal tankers, owners and chartering teams often want a measured view of the steel before taking a ship on, extending a charter or committing to a docking.

sections.h: Port state control and the rules that apply
p: Italy is a Paris MoU state, and port state control is carried out by the Italian Coast Guard, the Guardia Costiera, through the port captaincies, the Capitanerie di Porto. Inspectors focus on hull condition and structure, particularly on older ships, so current readings and a clear renewal plan help the ship at the gangway.

All Italian coastal waters lie in the Mediterranean emission control area, where the sulphur limit under MARPOL Annex VI, regulation 14, is tightened. That is a major reason scrubbers are common among Italian callers. As an EU state, Italy applies the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, which matters to owners of older ships deciding whether to repair or sell.

At Trieste, the cold north-easterly bora can be strong enough to hold ships off the berth, and winter gales affect the Ligurian and Adriatic coasts. Summer is cruise season at Civitavecchia, Naples, Genoa and Venice, so berths and quay space tighten and gauging aboard passenger ships is limited to the spaces the ship's management agrees.

Venice and the lagoon ports have their own traffic rules, with restrictions on large ship movements, so timing a gauging job there is a matter for the ship's agent and the harbour authority. Sicilian and Sardinian ports can be reached only by sea or air, so the team plans travel with that in mind.

sections.h: What a gauging job looks like on an Italian call
p: A typical job starts with the ship's thickness measurement plan and the last survey report, which tell the team which frames, strakes and tanks matter. The agent confirms the berth or yard slot, and the master confirms which tanks are cleaned and gas-free. On arrival the team marks the plan against the ship, gauges the agreed areas with calibrated instruments and records each reading against its location.

On an Italian call the main variable is time alongside. A container ship at Genoa or La Spezia may stay only a day, a tanker at Augusta may wait days for a berth, and a ship at a Sicilian yard may sit for weeks. The scope is sized to the real window, with the most critical areas first, so a short call still produces a usable steel list.

sections.h: Planning an Italian gauging job from India
p: The team travels from India for each job. Italy is a Schengen state, so Schengen visas are needed and the consulate sets the timeline. Work goes through the ship's agent, who arranges the gangway, port security passes and tank entry permits. We ask early for the thickness measurement plan, the ship's last survey reports and her confirmed berth or dry-dock slot, and plan the mobilisation around that firm schedule.

Several berths may be available to one ship in Italy, so the agent's confirmation of the actual berth matters. Readings, photographs and a steel renewal estimate are reported after the job, with preliminary readings shared on request while the work is in progress.

sections.h: Which services Italian calls ask for
p: Pre-docking hull and tank gauging comes first, as Italy has a deep bench of repair yards. Renewal survey thickness measurement support follows, then tanker cargo and ballast tank gauging at the refinery ports. Scrubber and ship piping inspection is growing because of the emission control area, and pre-purchase and on-hire gauging is common where ships are sold or chartered. Corrosion mapping on suspect plating can follow a first set of readings.

faqs.q: Which Italian ports can you gauge ships at?
faqs.a: Every port with a page in this section, from Genoa, La Spezia and Livorno on the west coast to Naples, Gioia Tauro, the Sicilian and Sardinian ports, and Trieste, Venice, Ravenna and Bari on the Adriatic and Ionian side. The best choice is generally the port where your ship is already due.

faqs.q: Is Italy inside an emission control area?
faqs.a: Yes. Italian coastal waters are inside the Mediterranean emission control area, where the fuel sulphur limit is tightened. That is why many Italian callers run exhaust gas cleaning systems, and why we routinely gauge wash-water and overboard piping alongside hull and tank readings on scrubber ships.

faqs.q: Do your technicians need visas for Italy?
faqs.a: Yes. Italy is a Schengen state, so technicians travelling from India need Schengen visas, with timing set by the consulate. We start once the ship's schedule is firm and plan the mobilisation around the confirmed arrival and sailing dates.

faqs.q: Can you work on a ship at a refinery berth?
faqs.a: Sometimes, for hull sections and tanks reachable from inside the ship, if terminal rules and cargo operations permit. Terminals set strict limits on hot work and tank entry, so the agent confirms what can run alongside cargo handling. Where it cannot, a separate lay-by or yard slot is simpler.

faqs.q: How does gauging fit with an Italian docking?
faqs.a: Gauging comes first. We take readings at the berth or anchorage before the ship moves to the yard, report a steel renewal estimate and mark the plates for renewal. The superintendent then agrees steel tonnage and docking days with the yard on measured readings.
